source.title: Improve SGD Training via Aligning Mini-batches
source.authors: Xiang-Rui Li; Deng Pan; X. Li; D. Zhu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an added training regularizer changes predictive performance and train/test loss, using ITDM rather than the specific interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper compares vanilla SGD with ITDM and reports test accuracy and cross-entropy, plus training and testing loss curves. ITDM is an added regularizer, but none of the versions names this method. The paper does not test random-label memorization, interpolation thresholds, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its proposed ITDM regularizer against momentum SGD. Its own results do not test any of V1–V8. Generalization and dropout are discussed as background; lower test loss from a different regularizer does not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: ITDM adds an MMD matching loss to SGD, is argued to reduce possible mini-batch overfitting, and improves classification and feature learning in their experiments. Their reported benefits are strongest for test cross-entropy; accuracy does not improve in every condition, and the proposed mini-batch-overfitting mechanism is not independently established.
record.recipe_differences: Adds ITDM, an MMD feature-matching regularizer between mini-batches, to standard SGD with momentum; uses ITDM-c in the main experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported accuracy varies with λ and dataset/model; cross-entropy is lower with ITDM at the reported best and worst λ settings. The paper states training loss rises as λ increases.

fits_no_version.finding: ITDM lowers reported test CE in every tabulated comparison except QMNIST, where CE is unchanged at reported precision. Accuracy gains depend on model, dataset, and λ, with some selected settings below baseline. The text reports increasing training CE with larger λ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding MMD matching of mini-batch feature distributions to momentum SGD can reduce test cross-entropy, while test-accuracy benefits depend on the setting and regularization strength.

record.problems: Main experiments train each model once on the train split. Tables report selected best and worst λ settings rather than all tested λ results; complete results are relegated to supplemental materials not included in the supplied text. Table values have no uncertainty estimates, although figures are described as having standard-deviation error bars. The reported evidence does not establish the claimed mechanism or a direct training-test error gap for every condition.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the selected best/worst numeric table results. Training/testing loss curves and other figure-only visualizations were not extracted as numeric rows because the supplied text gives no exact values for them.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that mitigate large-batch penalties; batch size is held fixed here.
Effects of adding, configuring, or removing dropout, including interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row values match the supplied tables. These are evaluations of the study's own method and should not serve as evidence rows for V1–V8. States are cannot_determine relative to those versions, not judgments that the ITDM differences are unreadable. Results average the last ten iterations; the main experiments train each model once, so figure error bars do not establish variation across independent runs. Tables 2–5 select settings by test accuracy, with corresponding CE values. The STL10 prose conflicts with Table 5 about accuracy drops; the recorded table values are retained. Figure-only results are already declared in rows_left_out and do not test a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test accuracy.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.
